parts.text: The IGCSE class is investigating reflection using a plane mirror. Fig. 5.1 shows a student’s ray-trace sheet with a line MR drawn on it. In the experiment the reflecting face of a mirror is placed vertically on the line MR . The additional dashed line shows a second mirror position. Fig. 5.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) NL is a normal to line MR . Draw a line 8.0 cm long from B at an angle of incidence i = 30° to the normal, below MR and to the left of the normal. Label the end of this line A . [1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) The student places two pins, P 1 and P 2 , on line AB a suitable distance apart for this ray tracing experiment. He views the images of pins P 1 and P 2 in the mirror and places two pins P 3 and P 4 so that pins P 3 and P 4 , and the images of P 2 and P 1 , all appear exactly one behind the other. The positions of P 3 and P 4 are shown in Fig. 5.1.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Draw the line joining the positions of P 3 and P 4 . Extend the line until it meets NL .

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Measure the angle α 0 between NL and the line joining the positions of P 3 and P 4 . At this stage the angle θ between the mirror and line MR is 0°. α 0 = .................................................... [2]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) The student draws lines at angles θ = 10°, 20°, 30°, and 40° to MR . The first line, at 10° to MR , is shown in Fig. 5.1. He repeats the procedure described in part (b) , placing the mirror on each of the new lines in turn. The readings are shown in Table 5.1. Table 5.1 θ / ° α / ° 10 51 20 69 30 90 40 111 50 130 Plot a graph of α / ° ( y -axis) against θ / ° ( x -axis). [5]

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) Determine the gradient G of the graph. Show clearly on the graph how you obtained the necessary information. G = ............................................... [2]

parts.label: e
parts.text: (e) In this experiment, when the mirror is moved though an angle θ , the reflected ray moves through an angle ( α – α 0 ). Table 5.2 θ / ° α / ° ( α – α 0 )/° 10 51 20 69 30 90 40 111 50 130
